news.headline: Cade (knee) questionable; Reaves (heel) and Nembhard (hip) out
news.detail: Cunningham sat Wednesday with a knee issue and is day-to-day. Reaves did a pregame workout that went well, but the Lakers have given no return date. Nembhard missed Wednesday with a hip problem.
news.take: Check each status before the daily lock. If IR is full, bench players who are out rather than leaving them in the lineup.

news.headline: Deni Avdija (foot) questionable for Thursday
news.detail: Avdija missed Tuesday against Minnesota with a foot problem and is listed questionable against Milwaukee. He has been playing about 33 minutes a night when healthy.
news.take: Start him if he is cleared before the Thursday lock (Friday about 8 AM MYT).

news.headline: Rui Hachimura and Isaiah Jackson are trending out of favor
news.detail: Josh Lloyd says neither needs to be held in standard leagues: Hachimura is shooting poorly from the field and Jackson has lost minutes.
news.take: Fair for deep benches. Hachimura still plays about 27 minutes, so he works as a short-term fill-in, not a long hold.

news.headline: Wendell Carter Jr., Jalen Smith and Coby White are must-roster players
news.detail: All three are still unowned in too many leagues according to the show. Carter brings rebounds and efficient shooting; Jalen Smith has a steady role; White adds scoring and threes.
news.take: Agree on the roles, but Carter has cooled over the last week. Hold, don’t chase at a premium.

news.headline: Sell Anthony Black before his minutes fade
news.detail: Black’s minutes, usage and steals have jumped while Orlando is short-handed. The show expects them to drop once the roster is healthy and suggests selling for any top-70 player.
news.take: His steals rate is unlikely to last. Sell if a fair offer comes.

news.headline: Sell high: Siakam, Norman Powell, Huerter and Saddiq Bey
news.detail: Siakam’s usage should fall when Haliburton returns; Powell’s surge comes from injuries around him and hot two-point shooting; Huerter and Bey are riding unusual block and shooting numbers.
news.take: Siakam and Powell are still useful starters, so only sell for clear value. Huerter and Bey are fine to move.

news.headline: Brandon Miller and Trae Young: slow starts, buy low
news.detail: Both are shooting far below their career levels. The show expects the percentages to recover and lists them as buy-low targets from frustrated managers.
news.take: Reasonable, but Miller is still ramping up after injury. Buy only at a real discount.

news.headline: Bridges, Josh Hart and Gafford are losing minutes
news.detail: All three have seen their minutes drop without an injury to explain it. The show says to act decisively when minutes and production fall together.
news.take: Bridges is down to about 21 minutes over the last week. Don’t trade a lot for him until his role steadies.

news.headline: Buy low: Zubac, Boozer, Ajay Mitchell and Gobert
news.detail: Their efficiency and minutes have dipped, but the underlying roles look stable. The show expects Boozer to finish as a top 30–40 player and Zubac back in the top 80–95.
news.take: Good targets if a manager is fed up. Don’t overpay; the bounce-back may take weeks.

news.headline: Jalen Smith, Ace Bailey, Jeremiah Fears and Moussa Diabate are must-roster
news.detail: All four have steady minutes and production that should last. Fears in particular is getting more usage with Dejounte Murray away from the team.
news.take: If any is on waivers in this league, he’s worth a claim.

news.headline: Jalen Green and Obi Toppin have lost 12-team value
news.detail: Both have reduced minutes and poor production. The show says to move on without waiting for a trade or role change.
news.take: Fine to drop for a steady free agent.

news.headline: Dylan Harper (hip) out; Julian Champagnie gains
news.detail: Harper’s injury looks significant. Champagnie moves into a bigger role in San Antonio and becomes a 12-team option.
news.take: Champagnie is a fair short-term add if a team needs threes and steals.

news.headline: Evan Mobley out 7–10 days (toe sprain)
news.detail: Cleveland will re-evaluate him in 7–10 days. Meleek Thomas and Tyrese Proctor get extra minutes meanwhile.
news.take: Managers with Mobley should bench him and stream a big for a week.

news.headline: Kawhi Leonard (knee) out at least another week
news.detail: Leonard has progressed in strength and conditioning but will miss at least one more week.
news.take: Hold him on IR if a slot is free; he’s a high-end player when healthy.

general.headline: Best week 5 schedules: Timberwolves, Trail Blazers, Knicks; Hornets play only twice
general.detail: Minnesota, Portland and New York play all their games on lighter days, which makes their players easier to fit into lineups. Charlotte plays only twice.
general.take: Matches the NBA schedule. Spurs and Clippers players are good streams too.

general.headline: Brice Sensabaugh and Quentin Grimes are hot adds, but only while starters are out
general.detail: Sensabaugh is near 30 minutes with Utah short-handed; Grimes is starting while Lakers guards are out. Both should lose minutes when teams get healthy.

general.headline: Dejounte Murray requests a trade
general.detail: Murray has been away from the team. If he is traded, players on both teams could gain or lose roles; the show advises waiting for the deal before making big moves.
general.take: Jeremiah Fears is the clear winner for now.

general.headline: Zach Edey is back: 23 points and 10 rebounds
general.detail: Edey had a big game in limited minutes, but his role could shrink as Memphis gets players back.
general.take: Hold if you have him; don’t trade a lot for one game.

general.headline: Thursday streams: Julian Champagnie, Kyle Kuzma, Trey Lyles
general.detail: Every Thursday game starts at 8 PM Eastern, so there’s no late-game window to react to news. Lyles becomes a strong option if Jonathan Kuminga sits.
general.take: Make streaming moves before the Friday morning lock (MYT).
